k1653:
A 2+1 apartment at Ish URT, an easily reached part of Durrës that has been lived in for decades.

The flat is unusually large for its layout: 145 m² in total, with 130 m² recorded on the certificate. It holds two bedrooms, a living room with the kitchen, two bathrooms and two big balconies.

It sits on the second floor — the first residential level above the ground — so the stairs are short and the balconies still clear the street.

The extra area is real living space rather than circulation, which is what makes this a family flat rather than a starter one.
k1654: Furnished 1+1 apartment on the ninth floor, Plazh
k1655: A furnished one-bedroom flat of about 43 m² net on the ninth floor at Plazh, in a managed building with a lift.
k1656:
A 1+1 apartment at Plazh, high up on the ninth floor of a building that is properly managed and has a lift.

It measures 50 m² gross and 42.95 m² net, arranged as a living room with the kitchen, a bedroom and a bathroom.

The flat comes furnished, so it can be used or let straight away without a fit-out.

At this height the outlook is open and the street noise falls away, and the sea and the everyday services of Plazh are both within walking distance.
k1657: 2+1 apartment by the railway station, Durrës
k1658: A 92 m² two-bedroom flat on the fifth floor near the railway station, in a managed building with a lift.
k1659:
A 2+1 apartment near the railway station in Durrës, one of the easiest parts of the city to get in and out of.

The flat measures 91.5 m² gross and 83.2 m² net: two bedrooms, a living room with the kitchen and a bathroom, on the fifth floor. The building has a lift and a management in place.

The layout does what it should — the rooms are usable shapes and little is given up to hallway.

The position is the argument for it: city transport, the main services and the routes out of Durrës all start from here, which matters more to a household than to a holidaymaker.
k1660: Three-storey private villa on a 400 m² plot, Arapaj
k1661: A furnished three-storey villa at Arapaj on a 400 m² plot, with about 105 m² on each floor.
k1662:
A private villa at Arapaj, in the quiet country south of Durrës rather than in the town itself.

The house stands on a plot of 400 m² and rises three storeys, with roughly 105 m² of floor on each level. It is sold furnished.

Three separate floors give a household room to spread out or to keep part of the house apart — for guests, for an older relative, or simply for the quiet.

Arapaj is countryside within easy reach of both the city and the coast, which is the trade a buyer here is making: space and privacy in exchange for a short drive.
k1663: Two separate 1+1 apartments in one building, Golem
k1664: Two one-bedroom flats of 60.2 m² and 55.2 m² on the fifth and sixth floors of the same building at Golem, 250 m from the sea.
k1665:
Two 1+1 apartments in the same building at Golem, sold together.

They are not joined: one is on the fifth floor at 60.2 m², the other on the sixth at 55.2 m². Each has a bedroom, a living room with the kitchen, a bathroom and a balcony of its own.

The building has no lift, which is the honest drawback at these levels and is reflected in what the pair costs.

The sea is 250 metres away and the mortgage paperwork on both is in order. Two separate doors in one building suit a buyer who wants to live in one and let the other, or to keep them for two households.
k1667: A 97 m² two-bedroom flat on the top floor of a managed building with a lift, in the quiet Pranvera quarter.
k1668:
A 2+1 apartment at Pranvera, a quiet and easily reached quarter of Durrës.

The flat measures 97 m² gross and 82 m² net: two bedrooms, a living room with the kitchen, a bathroom and a balcony. It occupies the fifth and topmost floor, and the building has a lift and a management in place.

Being on the top floor means nobody overhead and light from more than one side, which is what makes these flats worth more than the ones below them.

The layout is regular and the rooms take furniture without waste, so it works as a family flat or as something held as an investment.
k1669: Pasta factory as a going concern, Ish Këneta, Durrës
k1670: A small pasta factory sold as a complete business: production line, brand, packaging stock and social accounts.
k1671:
What is on sale here is a business rather than a property: a small pasta factory at Ish Këneta in Durrës, complete and ready to start work.

The production line is in place and set up to make pasta in seven different shapes, each shape represented by its own die.

The brand comes with it and has been built out properly — printed bags designed in Britain, of which more than five million are in stock, cartons carrying the logo, and accounts already running on Instagram, Facebook and TikTok.

In other words the groundwork a food brand normally spends its first year on has been done. What the buyer takes on is a business to restart, not one to build from nothing.
k1672: Third floor of a private house with terrace, Muzeumi, Durrës
k1673: A 100 m² floor of a private house at Muzeumi with three bedrooms, two balconies and a terrace of its own.
k1674:
The third floor of a private house at Muzeumi in Durrës, sold on its own.

The floor covers 100 m² and holds three bedrooms, a living room with the kitchen and a bathroom. It also has two balconies and a terrace.

Three bedrooms on a single floor of this size is generous, and the terrace adds outdoor space that a flat in a block would not come with.

Buying a floor of a house rather than an apartment means fewer neighbours and more control over the building, which some buyers prefer and others find unfamiliar — worth seeing in person before deciding.
k1675: 1+1 apartment steps from the sea, Shkëmbi i Kavajës
k1676: A 55 m² one-bedroom flat on the sixth floor at Shkëmbi i Kavajës, in a building with a lift and with the paperwork in order.
k1677:
A 1+1 apartment at Shkëmbi i Kavajës, a few steps from the water in one of the most sought-after stretches of the Durrës coast.

The flat measures 55 m² gross and 48 m² net: a living room with the kitchen, a bedroom and a bathroom. It is on the sixth floor and the building has a lift.

Light reaches the rooms through the day and the plan is practical, with nothing wasted on corridor.

The mortgage paperwork is in order. At this size and this distance from the sea, the flat is bought as readily for the summer or for letting as it is to live in.
k1678: 2+1 apartment with sea view at Blue Star, Durrës
k1679: A 130 m² two-bedroom flat on the sixth floor at Blue Star, with two bathrooms and two balconies facing the sea.
k1680:
A large 2+1 apartment at Blue Star, close to the Durrës sea front.

It measures 130 m² gross and 115 m² net: two bedrooms, a living room with the kitchen, two bathrooms and two balconies, both of which look out to the sea. The flat is on the sixth residential floor.

The orientation is favourable and the flat holds daylight through the day, which at this depth of floor plan is not automatic.

Bars, restaurants and shops are close by and the water is a short walk. The size puts it in family territory rather than holiday-flat territory, though it would let well either way.
k1681: Top-floor 1+1 apartment at the entrance to Durrës
k1682: A one-bedroom flat with 72 m² of internal space on the sixth and top floor, in a building without a lift.
k1683:
A 1+1 apartment at the entrance to Durrës, one of the easiest points in the city to reach and to leave.

Inside there is a living room with the kitchen, a bedroom and a bathroom. The internal space comes to 72 m², while the figure recorded on the certificate is 57.17 m² — the difference is in the structure of the building, and it is the larger number that is actually lived in.

The flat occupies the sixth and topmost floor. There is no lift, which is the plain drawback and the reason the price sits where it does.

In exchange, nobody lives overhead, the ventilation is good and the daylight is unobstructed.
k1685: A 62 m² one-bedroom flat on the fifth floor of a recently built block in Golem, within reach of the beach.
k1686:
A 1+1 apartment in Golem, in one of the quieter and more sought-after parts of this coast.

The flat measures 62 m² and is arranged as a living room with the kitchen, a bedroom and a bathroom, on the fifth residential floor.

The building is new, so the services and finishes are current rather than inherited, which is the main reason buyers here choose recent construction over older stock a street away.

The beach and the everyday shops are both an easy walk. A flat of this size in Golem is bought about as often for the summer as for the year.
k1687: 124 m² commercial unit with parking, Plazh Iliria
k1688: A 124 m² commercial space at Plazh Iliria with room to park four or five cars.
k1689:
A commercial unit of 124 m² at Plazh Iliria, in a developed and busy part of the Durrës beach area.

Parking for four or five cars belongs to the unit. On this stretch that is the detail that decides between one address and another, because customers who cannot stop tend not to come back.

The space is open enough to take an office, a showroom, a clinic, a shop or a studio without structural work.

Access is straightforward and the area carries trade through the year rather than only in the summer months.
k1691: A 72 m² two-bedroom flat on the fourth floor, not the top one, in a well-connected residential part of Durrës.
k1692:
A 2+1 apartment in Lagjja 17, a residential quarter of Durrës that is easy to get around from.

The flat covers 72 m² in total, with 60.4 m² recorded on the certificate. It holds two bedrooms, a living room with the kitchen and a bathroom, on the fourth residential floor.

It is not the top floor, which spares the flat the roof and the heat that comes with it in August.

The plan is functional and suits a family: the rooms are of usable size and the flat sits close to the services people actually use week to week.
k1693: 70 m² roadside commercial unit, Plazh Iliria
k1694: A 70 m² commercial unit on the main road at Plazh Iliria, with high visibility and traffic through the year.
k1695:
A commercial unit of 70 m² at Plazh Iliria, standing directly on the main road.

The frontage is what is being sold here as much as the floor area: passing traffic sees the unit, and customers reach it without leaving the main route.

The space takes a shop, an office, a studio, a service business or a small market without needing to be reworked.

The area keeps its traffic through the year rather than emptying out after the season, and the seller is open to negotiation with a serious buyer.
k1696: Apartments in the Kapiten residence, first line, Golem
k1697: Apartments in a first-line residence at Golem, ten metres from the shore, in a range of sizes and floors at one price per m².
k1698:
Apartments in the Kapiten residence at Golem, on the first line with the sea and about ten metres from the shore.

The building is close enough to the water that the sea is in view from almost every floor, which is the whole argument for a first-line address on this coast.

Units are available in different sizes and on different floors, and all of them are offered at the same price per square metre — so the choice comes down to layout and level rather than to what a higher floor costs.

The residence is due to be finished in December. Golem fills with holidaymakers through the summer, so a flat this close to the water lets easily in season.
k1699: Apartments in the Erdiar Residence, Qerret
k1700: Apartments of various layouts in a modern complex at Qerret, near Mali i Robit and close to the sea.
